profile.name: PostHog
profile.summary: PostHog sells an all-in-one product analytics platform that combines event analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, surveys, and a data warehouse. Its newer pitch is a context layer that automatically diagnoses problems, fixes bugs, and opens pull requests without being prompted. It is sold to software product and engineering teams that want one tool instead of stitching together several separate analytics and experimentation vendors.
profile.icp:
Buyer: Software and SaaS companies. The purchase is usually owned by engineering leads, heads of product, or product engineers, with data teams and founders involved at smaller companies.
Size: Mostly startups and scale-ups from seed to Series C, roughly 5 to 500 employees, with self-serve adoption by small teams and sales-assisted expansion at larger ones.
Signals they need it now:
- Job posts for product engineers, product analysts, or growth engineers that mention tools like Amplitude, Mixpanel, or Heap
- Recent launch of a new product or major feature that needs usage tracking and experimentation
- Job posts for a first data engineer or analytics engineer at a small software company
- Public complaints or posts about rising costs or complexity from multiple analytics, session replay, and feature flag tools
- Recent funding round at a software startup with an engineering team scaling quickly

prospect.name: Linq
prospect.fit: Series A ($20M) developer-facing messaging platform for AI agents hiring product and backend roles that need adoption analytics.

email.subject: Adoption analytics for Linq
email.body:
Hi Linq team,

Linq builds a messaging platform for AI agents, and developer products like that usually need to see where people drop off between signup, first message sent, and production use. PostHog puts event analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B tests and surveys in one tool, so product and backend engineers can work from the same data instead of stitching together several vendors.

It can also flag problems on its own and open pull requests for fixes.

Would it be useful if I sent over a short example of how a developer-facing product tracks activation in PostHog?
